question: What does a reasoning model's forced next-answer distribution do as progressively longer prefixes of one sampled reasoning trace are reinserted into a prompt, which trace properties account for the change, and can another model recover from or become anchored to a prefix whose induced answer is wrong?

key_findings.claim: The proposed trajectory probe is a sequence of textual re-prompting interventions, not a direct observation of one uninterrupted model computation or its latent decision state.
key_findings.evidence: For each item the authors first sample a complete trace, cut that fixed text at token deciles, append a model-specific early-stopping suffix, and run a new forward pass that must emit exactly one next token; the choice argmax and raw softmax are then treated as the answer distribution. At decile 100 this is still a re-probe of the sampled trace rather than necessarily the answer originally sampled with it. The suffix itself changes the context, although a shorter Qwen suffix gives qualitatively similar curves. Consequently the curves measure how a model responds when conditioned on trace text, not how an internal belief evolved during the original generation.

anchors.section: Appendix A / Trace generation and answer probing

key_findings.claim: Forced-answer accuracy rises substantially from no supplied reasoning to the full sampled trace for nearly every model-dataset pair, but the magnitude is model dependent and one endpoint is non-monotone.
key_findings.evidence: Across three runs, GPQA Diamond decile-0 to decile-100 accuracy is 30.8% to 54.4% for Qwen3-4B, 30.8% to 49.0% for Qwen3-8B, 38.4% to 62.5% for Qwen3-14B, 40.6% to 65.7% for gpt-oss-20b, and 42.3% to 73.1% for gpt-oss-120b. MMLU-Pro changes from 40.4% to 69.7%, 43.1% to 61.1%, 50.4% to 76.6%, 42.5% to 74.6%, and 46.4% to 79.4%, respectively. The Qwen3-8B curve falls from decile 90 to 100 on both datasets, contrary to a literal reading of the abstract's claim that accuracy consistently increases.

anchors.section: 3.1 Accuracy and decision commitment increase with reasoning depth / Figure 2

key_findings.claim: Longer supplied prefixes make the re-probed answer distribution increasingly concentrate on the answer chosen at decile 100, while non-choice mass and answer flips generally decline.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines decision commitment post hoc as the probability at each decile assigned to that question-run's decile-100 argmax, not as probability of the correct answer. Figure 2 reports rising commitment, falling non-choice probability, and falling consecutive-decile flip rates for most models; Qwen3-8B is again exceptional because its full-trace formatting changes the next-token distribution. This is evidence of endpoint convergence under the intervention, but because the endpoint label is defined from the same trajectory it is not an independent correctness or calibration measure.

key_findings.claim: Matched-length controls support instance alignment and token order as important, but do not cleanly establish that the gain is primarily semantic reasoning rather than answer-bearing text and distributional naturalness.
key_findings.evidence: At decile 100, original-trace gains over decile 0 are 18.1-33.1 points. Uniform random vocabulary tokens change accuracy by -3.9 to +4.2 points from decile 0; a different question's coherent prefix is -18.4 to +3.0; shuffling the same token multiset preserves +0.3 to +10.8. Original traces beat each control with reported p<0.001. Yet uniform random strings are far off-distribution, swapped traces may actively assert a wrong solution, and shuffling retains answer letters and lexical clues. These controls distinguish matched instance text from their chosen corruptions, but they do not separate inferential content from directly stated answers or other trace-local cues.

anchors.section: 2.2 Controls for context length, trace structure, and token identity

key_findings.claim: The experiment does not remove explicit answers from trace prefixes, so late-decile accuracy and cross-model transfer can include answer extraction or repetition rather than cumulative reasoning alone.
key_findings.evidence: The full sampled traces include conclusions and sometimes LaTeX boxed answers, and the probe requests one of the same option letters. No answer-letter, conclusion, or boxed-expression scrubbing control is reported. The Qwen3-8B anomaly demonstrates the sensitivity directly: about 27% of its full traces contain \boxed{}, P(A|boxed) is 82.2% on GPQA and 68.3% on MMLU-Pro, and boxed-trace accuracy is 44.2% versus 50.8% and 33.6% versus 71.6%, respectively. A later direct study, arXiv:2605.28913v1, explicitly finds that force-answer transfer can be driven by answer availability, reinforcing the need for such a control without retroactively establishing its magnitude here.

key_findings.claim: Additional reasoning is not uniformly beneficial even though aggregate accuracy improves.
key_findings.evidence: Comparing decile 0 with decile 100, the appendix reports that 7-11% of GPQA cases and 4-5% of MMLU-Pro cases move from correct to incorrect. Qwen3-8B also loses aggregate accuracy at the final decile. These disclosed negative outcomes qualify the paper's repeated language of consistent improvement and matter for any early-stopping policy.

key_findings.claim: The reported confidence analysis shows diminishing discrimination, but does not measure probabilistic calibration in the standard sense.
key_findings.evidence: Figure A3 compares mean probability on each decile's argmax conditional on that argmax being correct or incorrect. Confidence rises for both groups; the correct-minus-incorrect gap stays roughly stable on GPQA, declines on MMLU-Pro, and tends toward zero at decile 100 except for the Qwen3-8B formatting anomaly. No expected calibration error, Brier score, log score, reliability curve, or frequency-versus-confidence analysis is given. The authors' 'does not improve calibration' and 'overconfidence' interpretation is plausible but stronger than this discrimination-gap statistic alone warrants.

key_findings.claim: Short traces correlate with higher accuracy, but the paper does not identify a causal benefit of brevity.
key_findings.evidence: Accuracy stratified by trace-length quintile generally decreases for longer traces, and gpt-oss traces are much shorter than Qwen traces. The authors interpret this as difficult questions eliciting more reasoning and explicitly state that difficulty cannot be controlled because the datasets lack difficulty labels. Length also co-varies with model family, tokenization, and stopping behavior, so the result is descriptive rather than evidence that shortening a given trace would improve it.

anchors.section: 3.2 Instance-specific semantic reasoning drives accuracy gains

key_findings.claim: A target model can often repair a source model's induced wrong answer when allowed to continue reasoning, especially from early prefixes.
key_findings.evidence: The rescue analysis conditions on the source model's forced argmax being wrong at source deciles 20, 40, 60, or 80. On GPQA, immediate-answer rescue ranges from 20.8-34.1% at decile 20 and 16.4-24.6% at decile 80, while free continuation reaches 42.9-68.1% and 25.5-50.3%. On MMLU-Pro the respective ranges are 13.9-29.5% and 9.2-23.9% immediately, versus 46.4-69.4% and 21.2-45.4% with continuation. Averaged pairwise continuation gains are 17.5-36.6 points on GPQA and 16.3-43.4 on MMLU-Pro.

anchors.section: Appendix A / Model transfer and free continuation

key_findings.claim: Longer wrong-answer prefixes are associated with less rescue and more anchoring, but the design cannot isolate a causal effect of prefix length.
key_findings.evidence: Immediate GPQA anchoring rises from 27.5-50.7% at decile 20 to 50.2-66.1% at decile 80; free continuation reduces these ranges to 15.3-33.2% and 30.1-56.8%. MMLU-Pro rises from 28.3-42.2% to 56.6-74.8% immediately and from 14.2-23.9% to 40.2-60.3% with continuation. However, conditioning separately at each decile selects different residual error sets: late errors are likely harder or more firmly wrong. Later prefixes also leave less context budget for free continuation. The trend therefore combines prefix length, case selection, answer exposure, and continuation budget.

anchors.section: Appendix A / Decile computation and free continuation

key_findings.claim: The reported McNemar significance is likely anti-conservative because repeated stochastic runs and, in Table A4, multiple deciles from one question are pooled as if they were independent pairs.
key_findings.evidence: Table A2 uses n=594 for GPQA (198 questions times three runs) and n=36,096 for MMLU-Pro (12,032 times three) rather than clustering by question. Table A4 pools errors across deciles 20-80 and says it also pools three runs, so a question can contribute repeatedly. McNemar's paired test assumes independent matched units; repeated outcomes from the same question violate that sampling unit. A question-clustered bootstrap, hierarchical model, or per-run question-level test is needed before interpreting the very small p-values.

key_findings.claim: The paper is internally inconsistent about how many MMLU-Pro runs underlie the cross-model rescue results.
key_findings.evidence: The main setup says all experiments use three independent runs unless explicitly noted. Figure 4 and Figure A7 explicitly call MMLU-Pro a single run, whereas Table A4 states that its pooled cross-model rescue and anchoring summary is pooled over three runs. The paper does not reconcile whether the table reran the experiment, whether the figure caption is stale, or which replication count supports the associated significance claims.

anchors.section: 2 Probing the trajectories of reasoning traces / run policy

key_findings.claim: The empirical scope supports diagnostics for two open reasoning-model families on multiple-choice tasks, not general claims about reasoning faithfulness or deployment safety.
key_findings.evidence: The study covers Qwen3 4B/8B/14B and gpt-oss 20b/120b on GPQA Diamond (198 four-choice items) and MMLU-Pro (12,032 ten-choice items). The authors explicitly list the multiple-choice restriction, absence of closed frontier systems, decile coarsening, and lack of a faithfulness test. They also use unequal model-family context limits and recommended sampling settings, report no completion/truncation rate, and reduce each answer to bare uppercase next-token logits. Practical trace-handling ideas follow, but safer deployment is not evaluated as an outcome.

anchors.section: Appendix A / Datasets, models, context lengths, and probability extraction

method.core_idea: Turn one sampled chain of thought into a controlled prefix series and re-query answer probabilities at evenly spaced token deciles; then corrupt, transfer, or continue those prefixes to diagnose which text and which receiving model determine the eventual answer.
method.mechanism: For every model-item-run, sample a full reasoning trace; define decile d as the first ceil(dL/100) source tokens; append an early-stop marker and extract the raw one-token softmax over bare answer-choice letters. Record argmax accuracy, probability of the decile-100 argmax, non-choice mass, and adjacent-decile flips. Compare the prefix against exact-length random-token, other-question trace, and within-prefix shuffled-token controls. For cross-model rescue, select source prefixes whose forced source argmax is incorrect at deciles 20/40/60/80, normalize reasoning tags, re-tokenize in a target model, and compare immediate answer with free continuation; anchoring is the probability of repeating the source's wrong argmax.
assumptions: Conditioning a fresh forward pass on a trace prefix plus an early-stop suffix is an informative proxy for a decision trajectory.
A one-token bare uppercase choice has a comparable and meaningful logit representation across the five models.
Token deciles are meaningful progress units despite nonuniform reasoning-step density and cross-tokenizer differences.
The sampled full trace and its decile-100 re-probed argmax define a useful endpoint even when the originally sampled response or its formatting differs.
Uniform-random, swapped, and shuffled prefixes isolate length, generic reasoning style, and ordering sufficiently to attribute remaining gains to instance-specific content.
Conditioning on a wrong induced source argmax yields comparable mistake sets across deciles and model pairs.
Question-run and pooled question-decile observations are suitable independent units for the reported McNemar tests; this assumption is doubtful.
A larger model repairing an answer after free continuation reflects recovery rather than simply a stronger unconditional prior, answer extraction, or extra compute.

techniques.role: Re-prompts a model with 0-100% of one sampled trace in 10% token increments and extracts next-choice probabilities.
Closes the reasoning channel or adds a Qwen time-pressure suffix so raw answer-letter softmax values can be compared at each prefix.
Uses uniform random tokens, another item's coherent trace, and a shuffled same-token multiset to probe length, trace form, and order.
Decodes source prefixes to text, normalizes reasoning tags, and re-tokenizes them for same- or cross-family receivers.
On prefixes whose induced source answer is wrong, measures receiver correctness and repetition of that wrong choice with immediate answer versus free continuation.
Partitions no-reasoning to full-trace outcomes into stable-correct, gained, lost, and stable-wrong and measures local argmax changes.
Tests paired binary outcomes, although the implementation pools correlated runs and deciles.

evaluations.setting: Five open-weight reasoning models (Qwen3-4B/8B/14B and gpt-oss-20b/120b) on all 198 GPQA Diamond items and 12,032 MMLU-Pro items; three sampled traces per item unless the rescue captions' exception applies; token deciles 0,10,...,100.
evaluations.metric: Forced one-token multiple-choice accuracy, probability assigned to the decile-100 argmax, probability mass outside bare choice letters, and adjacent-decile argmax flip rate.
evaluations.result: GPQA accuracy improves by 18.2-30.8 points and MMLU-Pro by 18.1-33.1 points from decile 0 to 100. Commitment generally rises and non-choice/flip rates fall, but Qwen3-8B accuracy drops at the final decile because boxed formatting biases its next token.
evaluations.baseline: The same item re-probed with no reasoning tokens (decile 0); curves also compare model sizes and families.

evaluations.setting: Exact-length random-token, other-question trace, and shuffled-own-prefix interventions across deciles, with original traces and three runs pooled in Table A2.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy change from decile 0 and paired accuracy difference versus the original trace at decile 100; McNemar p-values.
evaluations.result: Random controls change accuracy by -3.9 to +4.2 points, swaps by -18.4 to +3.0, and shuffles by +0.3 to +10.8, versus original gains of +18.1 to +33.1; all original-versus-control comparisons are marked p<0.001.
evaluations.baseline: Original instance-aligned trace at equal token length and the no-reasoning prompt.

evaluations.setting: Cross-model transfer at source deciles 20/40/60/80, restricted to cases where the source model's forced argmax is wrong; receivers include larger Qwen and gpt-oss models in immediate and free-continuation modes.
evaluations.metric: Rescue rate (receiver correct), anchoring rate (receiver repeats source wrong answer), and free-minus-immediate differences.
evaluations.result: Free continuation improves average pairwise rescue by 17.5-36.6 points on GPQA and 16.3-43.4 on MMLU-Pro. Rescue generally falls and anchoring rises at later deciles; free continuation reduces but does not eliminate anchoring.
evaluations.baseline: Immediate forced answer from the same transferred prefix.

evaluations.setting: Full-trace Qwen3 formatting audit on both benchmarks.
evaluations.metric: Fraction producing \boxed{}, conditional probability of choice A, and accuracy with versus without boxed formatting.
evaluations.result: Qwen3-8B produces boxed text on 27.4% of GPQA and 27.5% of MMLU-Pro traces; P(A|boxed) is 82.2%/68.3%, and accuracy is 44.2%/33.6% boxed versus 50.8%/71.6% non-boxed. Other Qwen models box only 1.0-3.4%; gpt-oss does not.
evaluations.baseline: Non-boxed full traces for the same model and dataset.

evaluations.setting: Full-trace run-to-run variance over three independent generations.
evaluations.metric: Mean plus or minus standard deviation for accuracy and trajectory diagnostics.
evaluations.result: Most MMLU-Pro accuracy standard deviations are 0.1-0.2 points; GPQA is noisier, reaching 2.6 points for gpt-oss-20b and 2.9 for gpt-oss-120b. The small 198-item GPQA panel limits precision.
evaluations.baseline: Variation across the three repeated trace samples.

evaluations.setting: Correct-versus-incorrect argmax confidence across deciles and trace-length quintiles at decile 100.
evaluations.metric: Mean argmax probability, correct-minus-incorrect confidence gap, trace-token distribution, and accuracy by length quintile.
evaluations.result: Confidence rises for correct and incorrect predictions while the discrimination gap declines toward zero; shorter traces correlate with higher accuracy. Neither analysis identifies calibration error or a causal length effect.
evaluations.baseline: Correct versus incorrect predictions and shortest versus longest within-model trace quintiles.

limitations: Author-stated: only multiple-choice answers are tested; extending the next-token probe to multi-token or open-ended outputs is not demonstrated.
Author-stated: only two open model families are included, with no closed frontier reasoning system.
Author-stated: uniform token deciles can hide nonuniformly informative reasoning steps.
Author-stated: trajectory probing does not establish that chain-of-thought text faithfully reports internal computation.
Reviewer: the intervention exposes answer letters and conclusions and does not include an answer-scrubbed or pre-conclusion-prefix control.
Reviewer: model families use different context limits, generation budgets, temperatures, top-p/top-k settings, templates, and tokenizers, weakening clean family comparisons.
Reviewer: generation completion, maximum-token truncation, parse failures, and exclusions are not reported.
Reviewer: no cluster-aware uncertainty accompanies the pooled repeated-run/decile tests, and GPQA has only 198 unique questions.
Reviewer: free continuation is not compute matched across deciles because later prefixes leave a smaller remaining context budget.
Reviewer: safety and policy usefulness are proposed applications, not evaluated endpoints.
failure_modes: A trace can move a correct no-reasoning answer to an incorrect full-trace answer: 7-11% of GPQA and 4-5% of MMLU-Pro cases are lost.
Qwen3-8B often emits \boxed{} before the requested choice, strongly biases the re-probe toward A, and suffers a final-decile accuracy collapse.
Coherent reasoning from another question can mislead the model below its no-reasoning accuracy rather than serving as a neutral style control.
Receivers remain anchored to a source model's wrong choice, increasingly so among later-decile error cases.
Free continuation repairs many but not all wrong prefixes and may expend nearly the entire remaining context window.
Confidence on wrong induced answers rises with more trace text, so commitment can increase without correctness discrimination.
Bare answer-letter tokenization leaves substantial non-choice probability for Qwen models and makes formatting artifacts look like decision dynamics.
Pooling correlated observations can make statistical evidence appear much stronger than a unique-question analysis would support.
reusable_insights: Prefix-response curves are useful black-box intervention diagnostics when described as conditioning effects rather than latent belief trajectories.

Every trace-value study should include answer-scrubbed prefixes, pre-conclusion prefixes, semantically faithful paraphrases, and natural but irrelevant controls in addition to random and shuffled text.
Separate endpoint commitment from correctness: track probability on the correct label, eventual sampled label, and re-probed endpoint label independently.
For multiple-choice logit probes, audit all tokenizations and formatting prefixes and report probability over equivalent surface forms, not only one bare-letter token.
Cross-model continuation can be operationalized as a repair layer, but routing should account for error-set difficulty, anchoring risk, remaining context, and compute.
Repeated stochastic traces and multiple checkpoints from each item require item-clustered bootstrap or hierarchical inference.
Outcome transition matrices expose harmful overthinking that an average accuracy curve hides.
A discrimination gap is not a calibration metric; reliability curves, ECE, Brier score, and selective-risk curves should accompany confidence claims.
open_questions: How much of the decile curve remains after removing explicit option letters, boxed answers, and final-conclusion sentences while preserving a coherent rationale?
Do latent-state probes or logit-lens measurements during the uninterrupted original generation agree with the textual re-prompt curves?
Can semantic or step-based segmentation identify genuine turning points more reliably than token deciles?
What is the rescue-versus-anchoring curve on a fixed cohort of items that is wrong at every tested decile, with continuation compute held constant?
How do results change for open-ended numeric, proof, code, or free-form answers whose evaluation cannot be reduced to one token?
Does item-clustered inference preserve the reported control and rescue significance levels?
Can a routing policy predict when continuation will repair a prefix versus amplify or anchor its error without using the ground-truth answer?
How often are full traces truncated at 28,000 or 126,000 tokens, and do truncated traces produce different apparent trajectories?
Would semantic paraphrases, answer-preserving rationale edits, and counterfactual answer edits disentangle reasoning content from lexical answer leakage?

competitive_landscape.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational direct antecedent for intervening on chain-of-thought text and measuring whether answers condition on it.
competitive_landscape.difference: Lanham et al. manipulate mistakes, paraphrases, filler, and early answers to study faithfulness across tasks; this paper instead sweeps prefixes of a model's own long trace, adds matched-length corruptions, and studies cross-model rescue. The antecedent already cautions that answer changes under CoT intervention do not reveal the model's original latent process.

competitive_landscape.title: Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest causal-attribution antecedent for locating influential portions of long reasoning traces.
competitive_landscape.difference: Thought Anchors replaces individual sentence-level thoughts, samples 100 continuations, and combines black-box, attention, and causal-suppression analyses; the present paper uses one fixed trace's cumulative token prefixes and one forced next-token distribution, trading local causal resolution for broad model/dataset and transfer coverage.

competitive_landscape.title: Answer Convergence as a Signal for Early Stopping in Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct antecedent for measuring when an answer stabilizes during reasoning and using stability to stop inference.
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu and Wang operationalize convergence into answer-consistency, end-signal boosting, and activation-based stopping policies across five tasks/models; this paper is primarily diagnostic, uses token-decile re-prompts and eventual-answer commitment, and does not evaluate a deployed stopping policy or token-accuracy Pareto frontier.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Think with Confidence
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct confidence-based test-time reasoning-selection and early-filtering competitor using the same Qwen3 and gpt-oss families.
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepConf uses internal confidence signals to prune low-quality parallel traces during or after generation and reports accuracy/token savings on math; this paper measures raw forced-choice confidence along one trace and diagnoses discrimination but neither selects parallel traces nor demonstrates efficiency gains.

competitive_landscape.title: Stop When Enough: Adaptive Early-Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Training-free early-stopping competitor motivated by overthinking and redundant reflection.
competitive_landscape.difference: REFRAIN uses a two-stage redundancy discriminator and a difficulty-adaptive SW-UCB threshold and reports 20-55% token reduction; the present work provides decile diagnostics and notes lost answers but does not implement or compare an adaptive stop controller.

competitive_landscape.title: Thought Manipulation: External Thought Can Be Efficient for Large Reasoning Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct antecedent for inserting one model's reasoning into another and analyzing following versus rethinking.
competitive_landscape.difference: Thought Manipulation deliberately inserts smaller-model CoTs to reduce a larger model's output tokens and reports blind-following and unnecessary-rethinking failures; this paper slices prefixes, conditions on induced wrong answers, and quantifies rescue/anchoring rather than optimizing end-to-end efficiency.

competitive_landscape.title: Reasoning Relay: Evaluating Stability and Interchangeability of Large Language Models in Mathematical Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest pre-submission cross-model partial-trace continuation antecedent.
competitive_landscape.difference: Reasoning Relay truncates at process-reward/log-probability thresholds and evaluates hybrid mathematical chains with a PRM across Gemma/Llama providers and receivers; this paper uses fixed source-token deciles, forced answer probabilities, GPQA/MMLU-Pro correctness, and explicit wrong-prefix rescue and anchoring.

competitive_landscape.title: How Well Can Reasoning Models Identify and Recover from Unhelpful Thoughts?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct recovery-from-injected-thought antecedent and empirical counterpoint.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. inject four controlled classes of unhelpful thought and find weak or inverse-scaling recovery, including jailbreak implications; this paper conditions on naturally sampled prefixes whose forced answer is wrong and often finds stronger receivers can repair them, but does not know whether the underlying prefix reasoning itself is erroneous.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Reasoning LLMs Robust to Interventions on Their Chain-of-Thought?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current post-submission direct competitor testing recovery from fixed-timestep CoT interventions.
competitive_landscape.difference: Von Recum et al. apply seven benign, neutral, and adversarial perturbations across math, science, and logic and jointly measure accuracy and continuation-length cost; this paper focuses on naturally occurring cumulative prefixes, matched corruptions, forced-choice trajectories, and cross-model transfer. The later study more directly manipulates error type and quantifies recovery cost.

competitive_landscape.title: Reasoning that Travels: Dissecting How Chain-of-Thought Transfers Across Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current post-submission near-replication of provider-receiver prefix trajectories, including forced answer versus free continuation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Cheng et al. explicitly distinguish answer extraction, reasoning scaffolding, and receiver competence across AIME, MMLU-Pro, and ZebraLogic and show force-answer AIME transfer can be answer leakage; the present paper predates it and uniquely emphasizes wrong-prefix rescue/anchoring and matched within-model controls, but its semantic-causation claim lacks the later paper's answer-availability diagnosis.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors present trajectory probing as a systematic account of how accuracy, answer commitment, non-choice mass, and flips evolve with reasoning depth, use length/form/token controls to argue that instance-specific semantic content drives gains, and connect cross-model prefix transfer to rescue and anchoring.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper evaluates five open reasoning models on full GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro, supplies deciles of one sampled trace, adds three exact-length controls, and reports immediate versus free-continuation rescue and anchoring matrices. Its combination of dense answer-distribution trajectories, corruptions, and wrong-prefix cross-model diagnostics is broader than any one cited predecessor.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest defensible novelty is the integrated empirical panel: cumulative own-trace next-choice curves plus three token-matched controls and conditional cross-model rescue/anchoring on two large multiple-choice evaluations. Individual components are not new: CoT interventions and faithfulness tests (2307.13702), sentence-level causal attribution (2506.19143), answer convergence/early stopping (2506.02536), external-thought manipulation (2504.13626), recovery tests (2506.10979), and partial-trace model relay (2512.20647) all precede it. The novelty must also be narrowed from an internal 'decision trajectory' or primarily semantic mechanism to a textual conditioning trajectory, because explicit answer content is not removed, repeated observations are treated as independent in significance tests, and a current near-replication (2605.28913) directly shows answer availability can dominate forced-answer transfer.

reviewer_notes: Primary audit read the pinned 33-page extraction end to end, including references (PDF pp. 11-14), all setup/statistical appendices (pp. 15-17), Figures A1-A7 (pp. 18-24), every prompt/full-response example (pp. 25-31), and Tables A1-A4 (pp. 32-33). The rendered pinned PDF was visually inspected page by page, with full-resolution checks of protocol p. 3, trajectory/control/rescue plots pp. 4/6/8, and tables pp. 32-33; PDF page numbers and printed page numbers coincide. Exact target-version check on 2026-08-23: arXiv lists only v1, submitted 2026-01-30 16:45:16 UTC; the indexed PDF is byte-identical (cmp success) to the official exact endpoint https://export.arxiv.org/pdf/2601.23163v1 and both have SHA-256 ef4c3f8acdc92397b19bab8ea76a188b33aaebfcc2d3a4c58a0e79e67dff34a4. The indexed text has all 33 pages, no missing-text pages, and SHA-256 b789b901f592acbb5ab19e29657bce88c2dec34519610d5e61fe7638645e4902. Related-work searches were performed after writing the mechanism/evaluation summary using three families: (1) trace-prefix interventions, thought attribution, recovery, and cross-model transfer; (2) GPQA/MMLU forced-answer convergence, confidence, early-stop, and control baselines; (3) the paper's cited novelty terms and predecessors (Thought Anchors, Answer Convergence, Thought Manipulation, Reasoning Relay, and unhelpful-thought recovery), followed by current post-submission searches through 2026-08-23. Every listed competitor was checked on its official arXiv current-version page and pinned to the displayed vN/date; no title-similarity or secondary record is used. Contradiction/negative audit specifically checked the Qwen3-8B endpoint reversal and boxed bias, lost correct answers, non-calibration of the discrimination metric, confounded length relation, pooled-run/decile McNemar unit, answer leakage, and the MMLU rescue run-count inconsistency. Confidence is high for paper content and version/provenance, and slightly lower for causal interpretation because raw artifacts and cluster-aware reanalysis are unavailable.
